notes: the conformance contract's design: ONE suite, TWO green subjects (the semantic reference + the first real rail) — the level-3 rung of the maturity ladder for the realtime-transport concern (spec/evolution/gap-ledger.json GAP-001 advances from level 2 to level 3-on-local-rail)
the SDK is the published livekit-server-sdk 2.19.1, UNMODIFIED (no fork); its requestTimeout option is in SECONDS (verified against the SDK's own ClientOptions typing + TwirpRPC implementation)

the SIGSTOP/SIGCONT refusal injection freezes the server process — TCP connections stay open but no request is answered, so the adapter's bounded request timeout fires (the honest transient-upstream shape); SIGCONT recovers it with all upstream state intact

the independent room-list corroboration: the server's own listRooms() must hold EXACTLY the channels the adapter's effect log says are open-but-not-closed — the adapter's exactly-once observable cross-checked against the server's truth

the honest delivery semantics: data-channel effects are at-least-once at the transport level under client-side timeouts (a timed-out send may still complete server-side); the adapter's ledger converges the ACKNOWLEDGMENT (the retry under the same key returns the original) — the port's documented contract
